symbols.name: h
symbols.def: \(h\) is the macro label whose micro-action fiber is \(\mathcal X\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: \(r_x\) is the aggregate share of micro action \(x\) under macro action \(h\).

symbols.name: U_X
symbols.role: noise for the natural micro-action mechanism

symbols.name: q_{\mathrm{can}}
symbols.def: \(q_{\mathrm{can}}(x\mid c,h)\) is one fixed Equation-11 residual conditional law.

symbols.name: P_R
symbols.def: \(P_R\) is the joint law of \(U_C,U_X,B,S\), shared by every selector construction.

symbols.name: \sigma_s
symbols.def: \(\sigma_s\) replaces only the \(X\)-equation of \(\mathcal M_R\) by \(X=g_s(C,S)\).

symbols.name: Z_s
symbols.def: \(Z_s=g_s(C,S)\) in the augmented and high-level structural equations.

symbols.name: \mathcal I_L
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_L\) contains every hard intervention on an arbitrary subset of \(\{C,X,Y\}\).

symbols.name: \omega
symbols.def: \(\omega\) maps an intervened value \(X=x\) to the split intervention \((H=h,Z_s=x)\), maps interventions on \(C\) and \(Y\) identically, and leaves nonintervened coordinates unset.

symbols.name: \widetilde{\mathcal M}_s
symbols.def: \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_s\) is the bijective \(\widetilde\tau\)-relabeling of \(\mathcal M_s\) on endogenous variables \((C,(H,Z_s),Y)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal M_{H,s}
symbols.type: high-level recursive SCM with a residual coordinate
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M_{H,s}=\langle(U_C,U_X,B,S),(C,H,Z_s,Y),(C=U_C,H=h,Z_s=g_s(C,S),Y=B_{C,\delta_X(H,Z_s)}),P_R\rangle\); the observed high-level state is \(C,H,Y\) and \(Z_s\) is the compatible residual coordinate.

symbols.name: \Theta_h
symbols.def: The set of \(\theta_h\) values over \(\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{free}}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_L
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D_L=\{(a,b):a_c+b_x\le\mu_{cx},\ p^\top a+r^\top b=L,\ p^\top a=0\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_U
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D_U=\{(a,b):a_c+b_x\ge\mu_{cx},\ p^\top a+r^\top b=U,\ p^\top a=0\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\beta_n
symbols.def: \(\widehat\beta_n=(\widehat p_n,\widehat r_n,\widehat\mu_n)\) estimates \(\beta\) under a fixed law and \(\beta_n\) in row \(n\) of a triangular array.

symbols.name: t_n
symbols.def: \(t_n\) is the row-\(n\) term of the schedule \(t\).

symbols.name: \Pi_{\mathcal B}
symbols.def: \(\Pi_{\mathcal B}\) maps a neighborhood of \(\beta\) into the product of the two probability simplices and the response cube and equals the identity on feasible interior arguments.

symbols.name: \pi_n
symbols.def: \(\pi_{n,cx}\) is the row-\(n\) probability of the identifying response-study cell \((c,x)\).

symbols.name: P_n^\circ
symbols.def: \(P_n^\circ\) is the law of the observations in row \(n\), with finite-dimensional target \(\beta_n\).

symbols.name: \mathbb P^{(t)}
symbols.def: \(\mathbb P^{(t)}=(P_n^{\circ,(t)})_{n\ge1}\) denotes a least-favourable experiment selected after the deterministic schedule \(t\) is fixed.

symbols.name: G_{\mathbb P,n}
symbols.def: \(G_{\mathbb P,n}\) has the covariance of the row-\(n\) primitive influence vector under \(P_n^\circ\).

symbols.name: E_{\mathbb P}^{\star}
symbols.def: \(E_{\mathbb P}^{\star}\) denotes expectation under the multiplier law conditional on the row-\(n\) data generated under \(P_n^\circ\) in experiment \(\mathbb P\).

novel.justification: A randomized deployment can use a fresh device that reads recorded context but has no access to latent response types.
Procurement systems can enforce aggregate action shares even when privacy restrictions suppress their context cross-tabulation.

standard.name: conditional weak consistency of primitive resampling
numerical step dominates primitive estimation error

assumptions.condition: The cdf of \(\max\{|F'_\beta(G)_1|,|F'_\beta(G)_2|\}\) is continuous at its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile.

standard.name: continuity of the limiting critical-value distribution

assumptions.condition: The cdf of \(\max\{|F'_\beta(G)_1|,|F'_\beta(G)_2|\}\) is strictly increasing at its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile.

standard.name: local identification of the limiting quantile

novel.justification: This boundary-indexed class includes sparse multinomial deployment margins while keeping every finite-row selector coupling well defined.
Stratified randomized response studies with allocation floors satisfy this condition even as rare strata become less frequent across rows.

assumptions.condition: \(\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}}\sup_{\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{BL}}\le1}\left|E_{\mathbb P}f(\sqrt n(\widehat\beta_n-\beta_n))-E f(G_{\mathbb P,n})\right|\longrightarrow0.\)

novel.justification: Finite multinomial margins and bounded cell means satisfy such a row-Gaussian approximation under uniform moment and covariance control when effective cell sizes diverge.
Multiplier resampling of bounded finite-dimensional influence vectors provides this approximation over multinomial arrays with uniformly controlled effective sample sizes.

definitions.name: free-selector implementation class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{free}}=\{(\mathcal M_R,s,\sigma_s,\mathcal M_s,\mathcal M_{H,s}):\sigma_s\text{ and }\mathcal M_s\text{ are constructed from }\mathcal M_R\text{ by selector-equation replacement},\ \mathcal M_{H,s}\text{ is constructed by }\mathrm{def:macro\text{-}scm},\ S\perp(C,B),\ \sum_{c\in\mathcal C}p_cs_x(c)=r_x\ \forall x\in\mathcal X\}\).

definitions.name: margin-compatible selector couplings
definitions.construction: \(\Gamma(p,r)=\{\gamma\in\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal C\times\mathcal X}:\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\gamma_{cx}=p_c\ \forall c\in\mathcal C,\ \sum_{c\in\mathcal C}\gamma_{cx}=r_x\ \forall x\in\mathcal X\}\).

definitions.name: common low-level response construction
definitions.construction: Fix one law of \((U_C,U_X,B,S)\) with \(P(U_C=c)=p_c\), \(B\perp(U_C,S)\), \(E[B_{cx}]=\mu_{cx}\), and \(S\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\). Fix \(C=U_C\), \(X=f_0(C,U_X)\), and \(Y=B_{C,X}\) in \(\mathcal M_R\). For input \(\gamma\in\Gamma(p,r)\), set \(s_x(c)=\gamma_{cx}/p_c\), construct \(g_s\) by inverse transform, and apply only \(\sigma_s\).

definitions.name: typed state and intervention maps
definitions.construction: Split the augmented coordinates \(W=(C,X,Y)\) into observed coordinates \(W^o=(C,H,Y)\) and the residual coordinate \(W^u=(\ast,Z_s,\ast)\). Use \(\delta((c,h,y),(\ast,z,\ast))=(c,\delta_X(h,z),y)\), \(\widetilde\tau(c,x,y)=(c,(h,x),y)\), and \(\tau^o(c,x,y)=(c,h,y)\). For a hard intervention \(j\) on \(J\subseteq\{C,X,Y\}\), \(\omega(j)=(j^o,j^u)\) sends \(C=j_C\) and \(Y=j_Y\) to the same observed-coordinate surgeries, sends \(X=j_X\) to \(H=h\) and residual surgery \(Z_s=j_X\), and leaves every nonintervened coordinate unset.

definitions.name: selector-specific high-level SCM
definitions.construction: For input \(s\), define \(\mathcal M_{H,s}\) with common exogenous variables \(U_C,U_X,B,S\), common law \(P_R\), endogenous variables \(C,H,Z_s,Y\), and equations \(C=U_C\), \(H=h\), \(Z_s=g_s(C,S)\), and \(Y=B_{C,\delta_X(H,Z_s)}\). The observed high-level coordinates are \(C,H,Y\), while \(Z_s\) is the residual coordinate supplied in a partial projection. The intervention \(\operatorname{do}(H=h)\) replaces only the equation for \(H\) by the constant \(h\), retaining \(P_R\) and the equations for \(C,Z_s,Y\).

definitions.name: all-intervention partial-projection condition
definitions.construction: For \(u\in\mathcal D_{(U_C,U_X,B,S)}\), \(J\subseteq W=(C,X,Y)\), and \(j\in\mathcal D_J\), let \((j^o,j^u)=\omega(j)\). Let \(w_j^u\) equal the residual solution \(Z_{s,j}\), with \(Z_{s,j}=j_X\) when \(X\in J\) and \(Z_{s,j}=g_s(C_j,S)\) when \(X\notin J\). Require \(\delta(w_j^o,w_j^u)=W_j^{\mathcal M_s}(u)\), \(\delta(j^o,j^u)=j\), and \(w_j^o=\mathcal M_{H,s,[j^o]}(u,j^u,z^u)\) for every compatible nonintervened residual argument \(z^u\). Here \([j^o]\) is SCM surgery on observed coordinates and residual surgery is used exactly when \(X\in J\).

definitions.name: endpoint selector and SCM certificates
definitions.construction: For inputs \(\gamma_L\in\Gamma_L\) and \(\gamma_U\in\Gamma_U\), set \(s_{L,x}(c)=\gamma_{L,cx}/p_c\) and \(s_{U,x}(c)=\gamma_{U,cx}/p_c\), then instantiate \(\sigma_s\), \(Z_s\), and \(\mathcal M_{H,s}\) by \(\mathrm{def:common\text{-}response\text{-}witness}\) and \(\mathrm{def:macro\text{-}scm}\).

definitions.name: paired numerical-delta construction
definitions.construction: \(\widehat F'_n(g)=\{F(\Pi_{\mathcal B}(\widehat\beta_n+t_ng))-F(\widehat\beta_n)\}/t_n\), where \(\Pi_{\mathcal B}\) is a locally feasible correction into the product of the two simplices and the response cube, is applied after projection to \(\mathbb T\), and is inactive with probability approaching one at every fixed interior \(\beta\). The same draw \(g=G_n^\star\) is used for both coordinates.

definitions.name: rare-cell experiment class without tuning restrictions
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}=\{\mathbb P=(P_n^\circ)_{n\ge1}:\beta_n=(p_n,r_n,\mu_n),\ \min_{c\in\mathcal C}p_{n,c}\wedge\min_{x\in\mathcal X}r_{n,x}\ge\kappa_n,\ \min_{(c,x)\in\mathcal C\times\mathcal X}\pi_{n,cx}\ge\kappa_n\ \forall n\ge1\}\). Within each row, observations are independent, \(\mathcal C\) and \(\mathcal X\) are fixed, and \(\widehat\beta_n\) stacks the margin and response estimators. No condition on \(n\kappa_n^3\) or on \(t\) is part of this class.

definitions.name: schedule-indexed triangular-array paired confidence envelope
definitions.construction: For an arbitrary deterministic schedule \(t=(t_n)_{n\ge1}\) with \(t_n>0\) and \(t_n\to0\), define \(\mathrm{CI}_n(t)=[F(\widehat\beta_n)_1-q_{1-\alpha,n}^\star/\sqrt n,\ F(\widehat\beta_n)_2+q_{1-\alpha,n}^\star/\sqrt n]\), where \(\widehat F'_n(g)=\{F(\Pi_{\mathcal B}(\widehat\beta_n+t_ng))-F(\widehat\beta_n)\}/t_n\), both endpoint coordinates use the same multiplier draw, and \(\Pi_{\mathcal B}\) is the row-feasible correction.

definitions.name: schedule-split rare-cell face-switching handle
definitions.construction: Embed the endpoint LP in support-stratified feasible charts and localize its active primal and dual faces on the \(2\times2\) array \(p_n=r_n=(\kappa_n,1-\kappa_n)\), taking \(n\kappa_n\to\infty\) and \(\Delta_n\in\{0,\lambda(n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}\}\) for fixed \(\lambda\). For sufficiency, combine row-feasible perturbation bounds with Gaussian anti-concentration under \(n\kappa_n^3\to\infty\), \((n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=o(t_n)\), and \(t_n=o(\kappa_n)\). For procedural sharpness, fix the schedule first. If \(t_n/\kappa_n\not\to0\), pass to a subsequence and choose a boundary array on which the feasibility correction is active with nonvanishing probability, then calculate its effect on the paired critical value. If \(t_n/\kappa_n\to0\) while \(\limsup_n n\kappa_n^3<\infty\), use the zero or local contrast to test whether rare-cell noise prevents optimal-face localization. In either branch, establish an actual limiting critical-value or coverage distortion rather than only failure of a proof condition.

statements.statement: For every selector construction, the equations of \(\mathcal M_R\), \(\sigma_s\), and \(\mathcal M_{H,s}\) imply, without additional assumptions, that \(C_{\sigma_s}=C\), \(X_{\sigma_s}=g_s(C,S)\), and the following surgical response rule holds for every \(J\subseteq\{C,X,Y\}\): if \(Y\in J\), then \(Y_j=j_Y\); if \(Y\notin J\), then \(Y_j=B_{C_j,X_j}\). In particular, response modularity is an immediate consequence of equation replacement on every branch on which the \(Y\)-equation has not itself been replaced.
statements.justification: This lemma separates genuine selector restrictions from invariances already forced by the structural equations and intervention surgery.
statements.gap: The content is an internal semantic audit of the constructed SCM rather than an additional maintained condition.
statements.consumer: The projection theorem can invoke the structural branches without assuming its conclusion.

statements.statement: For every feasible selector \(s\), \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_s\) is the constructive \(\widetilde\tau\)-relabeling of \(\mathcal M_s\), and \(\mathcal M_{H,s}\) is its partial SCM projection in the sense of Xia and Bareinboim, Proposition 1 and Definition 6. Fix any \(u=(u_C,u_X,b,s_0)\), any \(J\in\{\varnothing,\{C\},\{X\},\{Y\},\{C,X\},\{C,Y\},\{X,Y\},\{C,X,Y\}\}\), and any assignment \(j\in\mathcal D_J\). The low-level surgical solution is \(C_j=j_C\) if \(C\in J\) and \(C_j=u_C\) otherwise; \(X_j=j_X\) if \(X\in J\) and \(X_j=g_s(C_j,s_0)\) otherwise; and \(Y_j=j_Y\) if \(Y\in J\), whereas \(Y_j=b_{C_j,X_j}\) if \(Y\notin J\). Under \((j^o,j^u)=\omega(j)\), the augmented high-level solution has \(H_j=h\), \(Z_{s,j}=j_X\) if \(X\in J\) and \(Z_{s,j}=g_s(C_j,s_0)\) otherwise, and the same \(C_j\). Its outcome coordinate obeys the required surgical split: if \(Y\in J\), then \(Y_j=j_Y\), equal to the high-level intervention value; if \(Y\notin J\), then \(Y_j=B_{C_j,X_j}=B_{C_j,\delta_X(H_j,Z_{s,j})}\). Thus simultaneous interventions involving \(Y\) and either or both of \(C\) and \(X\) use the intervention value and never the replaced response equation. For every compatible residual argument, \(\delta(w_j^o,w_j^u)=W_j^{\mathcal M_s}(u)\), \(\delta(j^o,j^u)=j\), and \[w_j^o=\mathcal M_{H,s,[j^o]}(u,j^u,z^u).\] Finally, surgery on \(H\) alone leaves \(Z_s=g_s(C,S)\) and \(Y=B_{C,\delta_X(H,Z_s)}\), so \[E_{\mathcal M_{H,s}}[Y\mid\operatorname{do}(H=h)]=\sum_{c\in\mathcal C}\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_cs_x(c)\mu_{cx}.\] Every selector uses the same \(\mathcal M_R\), \(P_R\), response-table law, and response equation; only the selector equation and its induced residual law vary with \(s\).
statements.justification: This semantic construction lemma makes the macro intervention and every surgical branch explicit before the transport image is formed.
statements.gap: Xia and Bareinboim give the general partial-projection identity; this lemma instantiates it for a calibrated selector family with a common low-level response SCM and selector-specific residual laws.
statements.consumer: The image proposition can attach a valid high-level SCM certificate to each feasible selector.

statements.statement: The compatible macro-mean set is exactly \[\Theta_h=\left\{\sum_{c\in\mathcal C}\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\gamma_{cx}\mu_{cx}:\gamma\in\Gamma(p,r)\right\}=[L(p,r,\mu),U(p,r,\mu)],\] and every point of this interval is attained by a high-level SCM from \(\mathrm{lem:projected\text{-}construction}\).
statements.justification: This supporting image and attainment proposition converts separate margins into the exact causal value set.
statements.gap: The finite transport image uses standard coupling geometry; its incremental content is the attainment certificate inside the displayed selector-specific SCM family.
statements.consumer: A PDX analyst can compute all responder means compatible with released tumor-profile frequencies and drug shares.

statements.statement: Two finite min-cost-flow problems compute \(L\) and \(U\). Optimal flows \(\gamma_L\in\Gamma_L\) and \(\gamma_U\in\Gamma_U\), normalized by \(p_c\) within each row, produce endpoint selectors, high-level SCMs, and all-intervention partial-projection certificates.
statements.justification: The bound must return allocations that can be inspected as causal implementations.
statements.gap: This is supporting finite transport machinery; its role is to make sharp SCM attainment auditable.
statements.consumer: A regulator can inspect the worst-case context-by-drug allocation and its corresponding structural model.

statements.statement: The following are equivalent: \(L=U\); every even alternating cycle \(c_1,x_1,\ldots,c_q,x_q,c_1\) in \(E_+\) satisfies \(\sum_{j=1}^q(\mu_{c_jx_j}-\mu_{c_{j+1}x_j})=0\), where \(c_{q+1}=c_1\); and each connected component of \(E_+\) admits potentials \(a_c,b_x\) with \(\mu_{cx}=a_c+b_x\) on every effective edge.
statements.justification: This supporting lemma gives the exact support-aware diagnostic for when the selector envelope collapses.
statements.gap: The alternating-cycle criterion is classical transport geometry and is not the headline contribution.
statements.consumer: An analyst can determine whether missing joint allocation matters before reporting bounds.

statements.statement: Fix a canonical residual kernel \(q_{\mathrm{can}}(x\mid c,h)\). It generates the unique coupling \(\gamma_{\mathrm{can},cx}=p_cq_{\mathrm{can}}(x\mid c,h)\), and therefore spans \(\Gamma(p,r)\) if and only if \(\Gamma(p,r)=\{\gamma_{\mathrm{can}}\}\). With positive margins and \(|\mathcal C|\ge2\) and \(|\mathcal X|\ge2\), \(\operatorname{dim}\Gamma(p,r)=(|\mathcal C|-1)(|\mathcal X|-1)>0\), so no single fixed canonical residual law realizes the free-selector envelope. The family in \(\mathrm{lem:projected\text{-}construction}\) satisfies Definition 6 selector by selector and makes no common Equation-11 Layer-3-map claim.
statements.justification: This supporting proposition records the exact quantifier boundary between a fixed canonical residual law and a free selector family.
statements.gap: The canonical Equation-11 construction determines one residual conditional law, not an entire positive-dimensional transportation polytope.
statements.consumer: An abstraction user can verify whether selector-specific residual distributions are admissible for the intended analysis.

statements.statement: If \(\mu_{cx}=a_c+b_x\) on \(E_+\), every selector has \(\theta_h=\sum_cp_ca_c+\sum_xr_xb_x\). Under full support this reduces to the standard version-irrelevance case in which changing a calibrated conditional version law cannot change the macro mean.
statements.justification: The reduction checks the criterion against a familiar special case.
statements.gap: The additive identity is classical; its use here is a sanity reduction for the selector envelope.
statements.consumer: It gives a transparent empirical-table validation check.

statements.statement: For every \(d=(d_p,d_r,d_\mu)\in\mathbb T\), \(F\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at the fixed interior parameter \(\beta\), tangentially to \(\mathbb T\), with \[L'_\beta(d)=\min_{\gamma\in\Gamma_L}\langle\gamma,d_\mu\rangle+\max_{(a,b)\in\mathcal D_L}\{\langle a,d_p\rangle+\langle b,d_r\rangle\},\] and \[U'_\beta(d)=\max_{\gamma\in\Gamma_U}\langle\gamma,d_\mu\rangle+\min_{(a,b)\in\mathcal D_U}\{\langle a,d_p\rangle+\langle b,d_r\rangle\}.\] The formulas permit non-singleton primal and dual optimal faces.
statements.justification: This supporting sensitivity proposition supplies the fixed-interior limit object when margins and response means move together.
statements.gap: This finite-dimensional formula is a direct specialization of Danskin and parametric linear-program sensitivity results, including Bonnans and Shapiro; it is supporting machinery rather than a standalone novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It diagnoses failure of optimizer-specific Wald calculations and supplies the endpoint limit law.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathrm{ass:joint\text{-}clt}\), \(\mathrm{ass:multiplier\text{-}law}\), \(\mathrm{ass:step\text{-}vanishes}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:step\text{-}dominates}\), the conditional law of \(\widehat F'_n(G_n^\star)\) converges weakly in probability to the law of \((L'_\beta(G),U'_\beta(G))\) at every fixed interior \(\beta\). Under \(\mathrm{ass:quantile\text{-}continuity}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:quantile\text{-}identification}\), \(q_{1-\alpha,n}^\star\) yields the pointwise simultaneous confidence envelope \([F(\widehat\beta_n)_1-q_{1-\alpha,n}^\star/\sqrt n,F(\widehat\beta_n)_2+q_{1-\alpha,n}^\star/\sqrt n]\), which contains \([L,U]\) with asymptotic probability at least \(1-\alpha\), including nonunique primal and dual faces.
statements.justification: This corollary makes the fixed-support envelope operational with one joint critical value.
statements.gap: The claim is a direct Hong--Li numerical-delta corollary after the endpoint derivative is established and is not presented as an independent inference theorem.
statements.consumer: A PDX analysis can report a simultaneous uncertainty envelope for the sharp lower and upper responder means.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}primitive\text{-}clt}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}multiplier\text{-}law}\), determine whether \[n\kappa_n^3\to\infty,\qquad (n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=o(t_n),\qquad t_n=o(\kappa_n)\] imply uniform simultaneous coverage for the row-feasible schedule-indexed procedure: \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P\in\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}}\Pr_{\mathbb P}\!\left\{[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\right\}\ge1-\alpha.\] The experiment class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) itself imposes none of these rate or tuning conditions.
statements.justification: This is the sufficient-regime half of the sole headline frontier for uniform inference with shrinking transportation margins.
statements.gap: Cho and Russell provide uniformly valid inference for linear-moment LP functionals through fixed nonvanishing random perturbations, and Gafarov provides uniformly valid sharp-set subvector inference under fixed positive rank and slack constants. Neither theorem establishes validity of this row-feasible numerical-delta procedure under the displayed rare-cell step window.
statements.consumer: A positive answer would give a usable tuning regime for simultaneous selector-envelope coverage when deployment and response-study cells become rare.

statements.statement: Fix a boundary sequence with \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\), \(n\kappa_n\to\infty\), and \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}n\kappa_n^3<\infty\). Determine whether the following schedule-quantified failure statement is true for the row-feasible paired numerical-delta construction: \[\forall t=(t_n)_{n\ge1}\ \text{with }t_n>0\text{ and }t_n\to0,\quad\exists\mathbb P^{(t)}\in\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}:\quad\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{\mathbb P^{(t)}}\!\left\{[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\right\}<1-\alpha.\] Use the two schedule-dependent branches in \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{unif}}\) on the \(2\times2\) array with \(p_n=r_n=(\kappa_n,1-\kappa_n)\) and \(\Delta_n\) zero or local at rate \((n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}\). A negative result is claimed only after deriving actual critical-value or coverage distortion. This question makes no minimax impossibility claim for any other confidence procedure.
statements.justification: This is the procedural-sharpness half of the headline frontier and has the required for-every-schedule, there-exists-experiment quantifiers.
statements.gap: Existing uniform LP confidence methods show that a failure of this particular tuning scheme would not imply impossibility of uniform inference. The unresolved issue is whether the proposed numerical-delta implementation has the stated rare-cell threshold.
statements.consumer: A matching failure theorem would tell practitioners when changing the numerical step cannot rescue this paired endpoint implementation even though rare-cell information still diverges.

statements.statement: Every compatible selector is superior to the reference intervention if and only if \(L>\theta_0\), and every compatible selector is weakly noninferior if and only if \(L\ge\theta_0\).
statements.justification: The lower endpoint translates the interval into a decision-relevant control comparison.
statements.gap: Béal and Latouche compare a known assignment algorithm with controls, not a deployment known only through separate margins.
statements.consumer: The PDX analysis can report whether responder-rate superiority survives every calibrated allocation.

sampling_model.design: For fixed-law supporting results, regular samples jointly identify \(p\), \(r\), and \(\mu\). For the headline questions, row \(n\) contains independent observations from \(P_n^\circ\), with fixed finite supports, target \(\beta_n\), and context, action, and response-study identifying-cell probabilities bounded below by \(\kappa_n\).
sampling_model.units: Target contexts and actions are multinomial draws; separate interventional response units identify every finite \((c,x)\) cell. Dependence across the stacked components is allowed through a declared row influence vector.
sampling_model.treatment: The response study observes micro action \(X\); target macro action \(h\) uses an unknown context-only selector calibrated to \(r\).
sampling_model.overlap: The class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) imposes only the floors on \(p_n\), \(r_n\), and \(\pi_n\), with \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\); it imposes no condition on \(n\kappa_n^3\) and no tuning condition. The sufficient question separately studies \(n\kappa_n^3\to\infty\), while the sharpness question separately fixes \(n\kappa_n\to\infty\) and bounded \(n\kappa_n^3\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The stacked estimator \(\widehat\beta_n\) obeys the assumed uniform bounded-Lipschitz row-Gaussian approximation, and its multiplier draw obeys the assumed conditional bounded-Lipschitz approximation uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\). The confidence procedure is indexed by an arbitrary deterministic schedule \(t=(t_n)\); the headline questions impose rate relations only within their own quantifiers.

Section 2.1.1, Theorem 1, Equation (4), gives a constructive sharp identified set for partially linear coefficients from unlinked outcome and covariate margins.
Causal consistency requires intervention behavior to commute across related structural models.
Constructive causal abstractions relate low-level and high-level models through state and intervention maps.

The COTA objective is jointly convex in causally constrained transport plans.

Methodology, Theorem 3.2, gives uniformly valid confidence sets for linear functionals defined by linear moment inequalities by bootstrapping fixed, randomly perturbed linear-program value functions; coverage over the exact identified set tends to one and exact coverage is obtained on an outer perturbed set.

Main Results, Theorem 3, gives uniformly valid confidence sets for sharp scalar projections of finite affine identified sets under uniform positive rank, slack, and moment constants, allowing multiplicity of primal optima.

tldr: The sole headline frontier is procedure-specific: whether \(n\kappa_n^3\to\infty\), together with \((n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=o(t_n)\) and \(t_n=o(\kappa_n)\), suffices for uniform simultaneous coverage by the row-feasible paired numerical-delta selector envelope, and whether every vanishing deterministic schedule fails on some \(2\times2\) array when \(n\kappa_n^3\) is bounded despite \(n\kappa_n\to\infty\). Cho--Russell and Gafarov already establish uniform LP inference by different perturbation or regularization procedures, so uniform LP inference itself is not claimed as new. The explicit projected SCM construction, sharp transport image, flow certificates, cycle additivity, fixed-interior sensitivity, and pointwise Hong--Li inference remain supporting infrastructure at incremental scope.

project_justification.gap: Cho--Russell give uniformly valid but deliberately conservative inference from fixed nonvanishing random LP perturbations, while Gafarov gives uniformly valid sharp affine-set projection inference under uniform positive rank and slack constants and allows flat primal faces. Those results do not settle the validity or sharp boundary of the row-feasible paired numerical-delta procedure when transport margins and response cells shrink.
project_justification.niche: The remaining field-level niche is a procedure-specific decay boundary with exact tuning quantifiers and an actual coverage-distortion sequence, not a claim that uniform inference for linear programs is new.
project_justification.fill: The project defines \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) independently of tuning, asks sufficiency under the only proposed rare-cell step window, and separately asks the for-every-schedule sharpness question. The two-branch \(2\times2\) handle distinguishes feasibility-correction distortion from optimal-face localization failure.

related_work: VanderWeele and Hernán show that multiple-version effects depend on a specified version-assignment distribution. Béal and Latouche apply that setup to PDX precision-medicine comparisons. D'Haultfoeuille, Gaillac, and Maurel, Section 2.1.1, Theorem 1 and Equation (4), characterize a sharp coefficient set under unlinked margins through transport; that result informs the discrete selector envelope. Rubenstein et al. and Beckers and Halpern inform the intervention and abstraction semantics. Xia and Bareinboim, Proposition 1 and Definition 6, supply the partial-projection condition instantiated by the semantic lemma; their Equation 11 canonical residual law is fixed and cannot span a positive-dimensional free-selector polytope. Felekis et al. inform the transport representation. Bonnans and Shapiro and Danskin directly supply the parametric linear-program sensitivity tools, while Hundrieser et al. study estimated-cost transport. Fang and Santos provide the general directional-inference framework, and Hong and Li supply the fixed-law numerical-delta corollary. Cho and Russell, Methodology, Theorem 3.2, obtain uniform inference for linear functionals defined by linear moment inequalities by bootstrapping randomly perturbed LP values. The selector interval embeds as one scalar partially identified functional, and their four lower and upper perturbed programs address both endpoints. Their stated class can accommodate finite rare-cell arrays under its boundedness and feasibility conditions, but their perturbation support is fixed and nonvanishing; coverage is one over the exact identified set and exact only on an outer perturbed set. Gafarov, Main Results, Theorem 3, constructs uniformly valid confidence sets for sharp affine identified-set projections, including flat primal faces, by regularized support functions. The selector envelope embeds in his finite affine system after one redundant margin equality is removed, but his uniform class fixes positive lower bounds on rank and no-overidentification slack; shrinking margins can leave that class, and his interval uses regularization and Bonferroni rather than the row-feasible paired numerical-delta critical value. Voronin provides delta-conditioned uniform consistency and pointwise inference for an LP-value procedure. These comparisons leave only the schedule-specific shrinking-margin boundary as the open novelty claim, with no assertion that uniform LP inference is new or that comparator assumptions are nested.
technical_internal_limitation: The selector seed \(S\) is atomless even though all endogenous and response domains are finite. The residual coordinate is endogenous with equation \(Z_s=g_s(C,S)\), which is essential for interventions on \(C\) to commute; its induced conditional law varies with \(s\). The result proves the Xia--Bareinboim Definition-6 partial-projection identity selector by selector and does not preserve one fixed canonical Equation-11 residual law or one common canonical Layer-3 map across distinct selectors.
honest_scope: The sufficient-regime and schedule-quantified procedural-sharpness questions jointly form the sole headline and remain open, conditional on the displayed uniform bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximations. The experiment class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) contains no rate or tuning restrictions. A failure theorem concerns only \(\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\) and would not imply minimax impossibility for other confidence procedures. Cho--Russell and Gafarov already provide uniform LP inference using different perturbation and regularization constructions. The projected SCM construction, sharp image and attainment, endpoint certificates, fixed-map obstruction, cycle criterion, fixed-interior derivative, and pointwise Hong--Li corollary are supporting theorem targets at incremental scope. No uniform theorem, failure theorem, comparator nesting, or fixed canonical Equation-11 map for the free-selector family is claimed.
